title: Priesthood ordinances make the power of godliness visible
setting: Joseph Smith moved from Hiram to Kirtland, Ohio, on 12 September 1832. Elders were returning from missions in the eastern states to report on their work. Joseph inquired of the Lord with six of them, and the revelation came over the night of 22–23 September. It was probably dictated in Newel K. Whitney’s store, with Frederick G. Williams as scribe. Partway through, the text shifts to address ten high priests.
summary: The revelation says the New Jerusalem and its temple will be built at the temple lot in western Missouri, within “this generation” of people. It traces the greater priesthood from Moses through Jethro, Abraham, Melchizedek, Noah, and Enoch back to Adam. It says this priesthood holds the key of the knowledge of God, and its ordinances show the power of godliness. Because Israel hardened their hearts under Moses, the higher priesthood was taken, and the lesser one continued until John the Baptist. It describes the oath and covenant of the priesthood: those who receive it receive Christ, the Father, and all the Father has. It says the whole church is under condemnation for treating lightly the Book of Mormon and the commandments. It sends the elders, called apostles and friends, to preach without purse or scrip, and warns cities that reject them. It assigns Bishop Newel K. Whitney to warn New York, Albany, and Boston, and ends with a promise of the Lord’s coming.

contextNote.title: What the greater priesthood is for
contextNote.text: The revelation asks what the greater priesthood is for. Verse 19 says it holds the key of the knowledge of God. Verse 20 adds that its ordinances make “the power of godliness” manifest. Verses 21–22 state the reverse: without them, that power is not shown, and no one can see the Father and live. Verses 23–25 give Israel under Moses as the example. The people would not endure God’s presence, so the higher priesthood was taken from them. In this passage, ordinances are the means by which godly power becomes visible to people in the flesh.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for section 84, “The Power of Godliness,” takes its title from verse 20. In verses 33–40, what does the Lord promise to those who receive the priesthood, and what are they asked to do?

newPeople.name: Aaron
newPeople.why: named in vv. 18, 26–34; brother of Moses, through whose line the lesser priesthood continued

newPeople.name: Abraham
newPeople.why: named in vv. 13–14 and 34; received the priesthood from Melchizedek

reviewNote: Read all 120 verses. Heading gives Kirtland, 22–23 September 1832, Joseph Smith and six elders, and returning missionaries. JSP historical introduction gives the 12 September move, the likely Whitney store setting, Frederick G. Williams as probable scribe, and the shift to “Eleven high Priests save one.” The six elders are not named in either source. Other biblical figures in the priesthood line (Jethro, Caleb, Elihu, Jeremy, Gad, Esaias, Melchizedek, Noah, Enoch, Abel) were not added as people; reviewers may want Melchizedek.
